HatchPattern__Blockwork__Meta.Meta__Description: Blockwork in section or on plan - diagonals at 45 degrees both ways, making a field of diamonds. Opener than the brickwork hatch so the two read apart where a cavity wall puts them side by side.
HatchPattern__Blockwork__Meta.Meta__WhyPaperUnits: Every length here is PAPER millimetres, like the dash patterns in Na__LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Config__.json, so the hatch measures the same on the sheet at 1:20 and at 1:100. Pattern scale adjusts from there.
HatchPattern__Blockwork__Meta.Meta__Spacing: Three lines each way to a 12 mm tile, so 2.83 mm between lines measured square to them (12 / 3 / root 2) - a third wider than brickwork's 2.12 mm.
HatchPattern__Blockwork__Meta.Meta__WhySeams: The lines run to the tile's edges and meet their continuation in the next tile exactly. No line passes through a tile CORNER and none runs along an edge: a corner is shared by four tiles and an edge by two, and ink there would need drawing by all of them. Na__LeHatch__SeamCopies paints what a neighbouring tile pushes across a seam, so a line keeps its full width where it crosses, at any line weight.

HatchPattern__Blockwork__Identity.Identity__Description: How this pattern is named, found and grouped in the pattern lists.
HatchPattern__Blockwork__Identity.Identity__Note: The standard section hatch for blockwork: brickwork's diagonals crossed by the same diagonals the other way.

HatchPattern__Blockwork__Tile.Tile__Description: The repeating cell, in paper millimetres.
HatchPattern__Blockwork__Tile.Tile__Note: Square, so both sets of diagonals close on themselves.

HatchPattern__Blockwork__Defaults.Defaults__Description: What the pattern draws with until a use sets its own. The stroke is 0.25 pt (0.0882 mm) at scale 1 and grows with the pattern scale; a line weight typed in the panel does not. 'inherit' takes the colour of whatever carries the hatch - a vector's edge colour - until a pattern colour is picked.

HatchPattern__Blockwork__Glyphs.Glyphs__Description: Drawn about the glyph's own origin, y pointing DOWN, in tile millimetres. Strokes only: the PDF stamps a tile as lines and never fills one.

Rising.Glyph__Note: Six pieces of three endless lines, x + y = 2, 6 and 10.

Falling.Glyph__Note: Six pieces of three endless lines, x - y = 1, 5 and 9 - one millimetre out of step with the rising set, so the two never cross ON a tile edge.

HatchPattern__Blockwork__Bounds.Bounds__Description: How far a use may scale and turn this pattern before it stops reading as the material.
